_readme: Retry batch after Gutenberg 504 outage cleared; 12 of 14 sourced with real text, 2 (Man Versus the State, Sanditon) confirmed genuinely absent from Gutenberg's catalog.

books.title: The Lady from the Sea
books.author: Henrik Ibsen
books.synopsis: Ellida Wangel, restless and drawn back to the sea, must choose between the mysterious sailor who once claimed her and the husband who finally lets her choose freely. Ibsen's play on marriage as bondage versus chosen commitment.

books.title: Salome
books.author: Oscar Wilde
books.synopsis: Herod's stepdaughter Salome, spurned by the imprisoned prophet Jokanaan, dances for her stepfather and demands the prophet's head on a silver charger. Wilde's decadent one-act tragedy, banned in England before its French premiere.

books.title: Vera; or, The Nihilists
books.author: Oscar Wilde
books.synopsis: A Russian peasant girl turned Nihilist conspirator is chosen to assassinate the new, secretly reformist Tsar, only to discover he is the man she loves. Wilde's first play, a melodrama of revolution and sacrifice.

books.title: Discourses on the First Decade of Titus Livius
books.author: Niccolò Machiavelli
books.synopsis: Machiavelli works through Livy's history of early Rome book by book, drawing out the practical lessons for building and preserving a free republic.

books.title: History of Florence
books.author: Niccolò Machiavelli
books.synopsis: Machiavelli's history of Florence from its Roman origins through the rise of the Medici, tracing the factional struggles that shaped the republic.

books.title: Past and Present
books.author: Thomas Carlyle
books.synopsis: Carlyle sets a 12th-century monastery's ordered, purposeful life under Abbot Samson against the chaos and 'cash nexus' of industrial Victorian England, demanding real leadership over laissez-faire drift.

books.title: Unto This Last, and Other Essays on Political Economy
books.author: John Ruskin
books.synopsis: Ruskin attacks classical political economy's treatment of workers as mere mechanisms, arguing that true wealth is the life and just relations it enables, not accumulation for its own sake.

books.title: Culture and Anarchy
books.author: Matthew Arnold
books.synopsis: Arnold argues for 'culture' — pursuing human perfection through the best that has been thought and said — as the antidote to class self-interest and the modern cult of 'doing as one likes.'

books.title: A Modern Utopia
books.author: H. G. Wells
books.synopsis: A philosopher and his companion, walking in the Alps, step through into a parallel Earth organized as a rationally planned world-state, and debate how such a utopia could actually be governed and kept free.

books.title: The Watsons
books.author: Jane Austen
books.synopsis: Emma Watson, raised in comfort by a wealthy aunt, returns to her poor clergyman father's household and must navigate courtship and family friction with almost no fortune of her own. Austen's unfinished fragment, abandoned after her father's death.

books.title: A Sicilian Romance
books.author: Ann Radcliffe
books.synopsis: Sisters Julia and Emilia Mazzini, raised believing their mother long dead, uncover a hidden wing of their father's castle and the truth of a mother imprisoned rather than buried.

books.title: Caleb Williams
books.author: William Godwin
books.synopsis: A young servant, Caleb Williams, discovers that his admired employer Falkland once committed a murder, and is hunted, framed, and imprisoned across England once Falkland realizes his secret is known.
